name: English
note: The catalogue (tools/i18n-extract.mjs writes it; do not edit). Each key is the English; a key `context::ENGLISH` is one meaning of a word that has two. `strings` is English itself as a pack (a plural key holds its English forms); `notes` says what a key means where that is not obvious; `names` are names, never translated; `sources` says where each key is used. docs/LANGUAGES.md §11 and FOR-TRANSLATORS say how to fill a pack.

notes.SQR: waveform names (saw up, saw down, sine, triangle, square, sample-and-hold, a slow random drift); most languages keep these as written
notes.STARTER: a preset the app ships (a starter project's modulation), not one the user saved
notes.STATUS TAGS: the small status labels over the picture (BASINS' badges and stats bar)
notes.STRETCH TO CLIP · SHIFT+T: a clip's menu: the file plays / the envelope alone / fit the audio into the clip's length (varispeed)
notes.STUTTER {note} latched — applies to BPM-: STUTTER: the clock holds the current beat and repeats it at the note value {note} (1/4 or 1)
notes.Selection scope: what a selection picks: whole clips or curve points
notes.Step through twelve density levels to re: shells: the nested surfaces of equal density in the picture (like the layers of an onion)
notes.Stutter: hold the beat at this note valu: STUTTER: hold the current beat and repeat it at this note value (a quarter note, a whole beat) while held
notes.THEME: THEME: LIGHT, DARK or SYSTEM, the light or dark mode (not the SKIN)
notes.TIME: the head of a device's left column: the shape PRESETs, the envelope TIME, the audio SOURCE
notes.TONE: a colour variant of the chosen theme (its tones have names, kept as written)
notes.TRI: waveform names (saw up, saw down, sine, triangle, square, sample-and-hold, a slow random drift); most languages keep these as written
notes.TRIG: short for TRIGGER: restart the curve on a trigger
notes.TRIGGER: the two kinds of macro: KNOB (a value you turn) and TRIGGER (a button that fires)
notes.TURN: a demo LFO's name: it turns the picture once per bar (the user can rename it)
notes.The controls take the panes’ light: one: the relief follows the pane light's ANGLE: one light for the whole interface
notes.The {panel} panel could not be built: {w: an error notice: {panel} is a panel's name (RENDER …), {why} the program's reason, left as it is
notes.This device’s tier, measured once: A and: a short benchmark sorts this device into tier A, B or C
notes.WALL: the clock follows wall-clock time (real elapsed seconds), as opposed to FREE, which counts frame time and slows with the picture
notes.clock state::HOLD: — the modulation clock is held (paused in place), as opposed to RUN
notes.close ({key}): {key} is the notebook’s shortcut key, e.g. J
notes.device view::FULL: a device's view: FULL shows every control, CMP (compact) only the performance bank
notes.dismiss: put the notice away (not close a window)

{inline} and {display} are the maths syntax, $inline$ and $$display$$, shown exactly as typed
notes.open {path} in your notes tab: your notes tab is the notebook’s first tab: the note you are writing, kept in this browser
notes.patch copied — {:PASTE} onto any {kind}: a patch: all of one device’s settings together, as a synth patch; {kind} is the device kind (LFO, ENV, AUDIO)
notes.peak hold::HOLD: the audio follower's PEAK HOLD: how long a band's peak is held before it falls (a time), not the envelope stage
notes.retrying without the processing constrai: the microphone's state: a browser that cannot turn AGC off is still worth listening to
notes.right rack scroll: the scrollbar beside the cards of the left / right RACK (the column of docked windows)
notes.search windows: the finder's search field: type part of a window's name
notes.text ink::SAMPLED: TEXT (the label ink) set by the app itself, from the picture under each label: "measured", not "a sample"
notes.the expander: the transport bar's expander: the panel under the bar with the macros, the clock and the app's own rows
notes.the gate opens here and stays open until: hysteresis: a small margin below the opening level, so the gate does not flicker open and shut
notes.the left rack: the RACK: the column of docked windows at the screen’s edge (not the SHELF, where notes are kept)
notes.the rack: the RACK: the column of docked windows at the screen’s edge (not the SHELF, where notes are kept)
notes.this page — markdown, {inline} and {disp: {inline} and {display} are the maths syntax, shown exactly as typed
notes.this place takes {accept}; that is a {ki: {accept} and {kind} are kinds of MIR file (project, page …), written as their ids
notes.time span::WINDOW: a span of time (in seconds) the view looks across, not an interface window
notes.waiting for permission to use the microp: the microphone's state: the permission prompt is up
notes.window {s} s: a window of time: the envelope graph now spans {s} seconds
notes.{band} · A {a} · R {r} · H {h} ms: A, R and H are the initials of ATTACK, RELEASE and HOLD (the peak hold), each in milliseconds: use the initials of your own labels
notes.{kind} {id}: a device's name: its kind and its id (LFO s2); reorder if your language puts the id first
notes.{kind} {name}: what drives a macro: a device (its kind and name, e.g. LFO 2), or HAND — the value set by hand, nothing modulating it
notes.{kind} — {message}: a status line: the device kind (LFO, ENV, AUDIO), then a message that is already a whole sentence
notes.{verb} — {what}: a button's name: its label, then what it acts on (SAVE — this project)
notes.{what} {i} name — type your own: the name field of a macro or a trigger: {what} is Macro or Trigger, {i} its number
notes.{what} · TIMELINE: a history row: what was done, then the window it was done in
notes.λWAVES: the app's name: keep it exactly as written
